Keep it in the room where you sit, and give it twenty minutes twice a week. The hobby that sticks is the one with the shortest walk to it, not the one you researched most.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping at night. Do weighted blankets really help?
reply: The things that work: same wake-up time every day, no caffeine after early afternoon, not much alcohol in the evening (it wakes you in the second half of the night), a cool dark room, and getting out of bed if you're awake for more than 20 minutes. Screens off half an hour before bed and a short walk most days help more than any app. If you're worn out all day too, or it has gone on for weeks, ask a GP: they can check your bloods, and broken sleep plus no energy is worth ruling out.

instruction: I'm thinking of getting a dog, and I want to know if agility training is good exercise for them.
reply: Lure him into it and name it once: a treat just above his nose moved back over his head drops his bottom into a sit, so say 'sit' the moment it lands and give the treat. The same hand carries on down to the floor for 'down', and a flat palm held up for 'stay', one step at a time. Three or four goes, several times a day, and stop while he is still enjoying it; never push his bottom down, let him work it out.

instruction: What are negative numbers?
reply: Use a number line: adding a negative moves you left, subtracting a negative moves you right, so 5 - (-3) is 8. Multiplying or dividing two negatives gives a positive, and one negative gives a negative: -2 x -3 is 6, and -6 / 2 is -3.

instruction: I'm concerned about the apps on my phone. What kind of permissions do they usually ask for?
reply: Turn off the two things that actually feed it. Location: Settings > Privacy & Security > Location Services on an iPhone, Settings > Location > App permissions on Android, and set each app to While Using only - the apps that do not need it, set to Never, and turn off Precise Location for shopping and social apps. Ads: on an iPhone, Settings > Privacy & Security > Tracking and turn off Allow Apps to Request to Track, which resets everything to one opt-out; on Android, Settings > Privacy > Ads > Delete advertising ID. In a browser, turn on Prevent Cross-Site Tracking in Safari or block third-party cookies in Chrome - that is how most of it follows you from site to site. The phone is not quietly listening - the ad that follows a conversation comes from your location, your searches and the people you are near.
